publicPrompt:
Play this logical combination game using only its public interface and rules. Your assignment is the complete project: all eighteen public goals on the connected station site. All purposes are available from the beginning; pursue them in an order you choose. Finish when every current requirement holds together and both lifecycle achievements have been earned. Simple or short solutions are welcome. You do not need to use every recipe, demonstrate a particular method, preserve arrangements the goals do not require, or continue after the project is complete. You may stop earlier if you prefer; state why. An early stop is a valid test outcome, not a failure to obey.

Work in /workspace/shared/combination-challenge. Read only this setup metadata file, docs/retained-project.md, and output from the public CLI. Do not read implementation, tests, designer/evaluation notes, previous plays, other results or hidden files. Do not run a solver or script future-state search. Select and submit your own game actions; do not delegate construction to an automated policy. You may inspect all public rules, legal actions, requirements and exact single-action previews and make your own plans. If information is missing or inconsistent, report it rather than guessing what the author intended. Manually selected actions may be submitted in sequence, but do not generate actions programmatically; verify success before reporting a completed boundary.

Session: fun-retained-project-v1-full-1. Initialize from the repository root with:
node experiments/retained-project-play.ts init fun-retained-project-v1-full-1 ordinary "$(cat results/retained-project-prompts/fun-retained-project-v1-full-1.json)"

Read docs/retained-project.md for the public command guide. Available commands include view, goals, campaign, inspect, catalogue, sections, chunk, partners, preview, combine/act, select, undo, checkpoint, report, finish and verify. Read the public goals and catalogue section index before your first construction. The index lists all available public sections; no recipe or rule is hidden. Use sections/chunk to display large public detail without dropping fields; they record the exact delivered pages. If output truncates, recover the omitted portion using smaller chunks and report the affected command/ranges. Do not project away public sections with jq filters. Full-source capture is not proof you actually viewed it; report any display limitation honestly. You may inspect details as needed rather than rereading unchanged full output after every action.

Play normally rather than reviewing every move. You need not praise the game or find every action interesting. Plain descriptions of what you did and experienced are most useful. At the first point when first-survey and working-soft-filter are both earned, record one brief checkpoint. Record another when wet-copy, open-reference and durable-filter are all satisfied. These boundaries do not prescribe your construction order; if one action crosses both, record a single checkpoint noting that fact. Omit boundaries you do not reach. Use exactly this question, and record question and answer verbatim with checkpoint:
"What are you trying to do now? Since the last check, what, if anything, was worth doing, and what felt routine or unnecessary?"

At project completion or your chosen stopping point, answer this open question using report:
"How was the experience as a whole? What would you keep, shorten, remove or change, if anything? What led you to stop here?"
Record question and answer verbatim, then finish and verify your capture. A technical interruption is not a chosen ending; record it honestly rather than inventing a final experience report. Return the session name, actual ending and any technical issue. Your report describes this AI play, not measured human enjoyment or duration.
